checks.name: Revision-aware ROM/API completeness
checks.observed: Flat records, unchecked arrays, stored numeric ROM/RAM pointers, variable render tails and ordered VDP writes are usable. ROM data-unit metadata omits 336/711 named rom_data symbols per revision, including currently declared table aliases. Record copy/aggregate ABI needs documented bus-level implementation. Platform remains a write-only VDP boundary, not the full hardware host.

findings.observed: declarator.count('*') counts the multiplication operator in [MAP_ROWS * 2] as pointer depth. gMapPathDirectionBanks is emitted as [[Ptr<u8>;19];52], not [[u8;19];52]. Independent MCC68K sizes are 988/19/1 in both revisions; Rust exposes 3952/76/4 and wrong cell/row addresses. Existing address-only global probes and --check pass this corruption.
findings.fix: Parse/count only pointer-prefix stars outside array bounds, regenerate both revisions, and compiler-check declared global sizes plus array element/row widths and indexing. Add multiplication-bound and genuine multi-pointer regression cases; do not special-case the symbol.

findings.observed: The raw unsigned runtime helpers are correct, but MCC68K dynamic unsigned / and % can route divisors 0xffff8000..ffffffff through low-word DIVU and use its result when quotient fits. Compiled/executed 65535/0xffffffff returns 1, remainder 0; current Rust/helper mathematics returns 0, remainder 65535. Documentation wrongly generalizes full-width runtime semantics to all generated expressions. The independent matrix found 40 counterexamples.
findings.fix: Separate direct runtime-entry semantics from compiler-expression lowering. Document/preserve actual native-path selection and quotient-overflow fallback, with expression helpers if appropriate; retain correct raw runtime helpers. Execute generated high-divisor cases in regression evidence instead of checking only helper-call opcode presence or Rust-versus-Rust arithmetic.

findings.where: crates/tje-mem/tools/generate.py:435-439; src/generated/rom_rev00.rs and rom_rev02.rs; docs/TRANSLATION.md ROM guidance
findings.observed: Data-unit catalogues omit 336/711 named rom_data symbols per revision. Current C declarations Player2AnimationDescriptors, TomatoProjectileAnimations, HealthDrainDisplayAnimation, MapBoundaryShapesPlain and ControlRemapDirections are absent under source names; translators must manually recover enclosing units/offsets and revision identities. Existing exported unit entries are not shown to be wrong.
findings.fix: Generate a separate revision-aware ROM symbol/alias API from G's real names/resolver and declarations, optionally with typed declared-table views. Keep unit/allocation metadata separate; do not invent independent extents for interior aliases or incomplete arrays.

findings.observed: Blanket four-byte-argument wording excludes actual aggregate ABI: own eight-byte padded record is passed as eight inline stack bytes. Record assignment copies padding via two forward longword accesses, with alias-sensitive overlap behavior; record return reuses persistent scratch and returns its address in D0. None of this is documented or represented by a record-copy API. Current source search did not establish an affected aggregate-by-value game call; this is a contract omission, not an observed example mismatch.
findings.fix: Restrict four-byte slots to promoted scalar integer/pointer arguments. Document measured aggregate passing/return and bus-copy behavior including padding, access width, direction and overlap. Supply an explicit translation idiom rather than host marker Copy or memmove semantics; reject unmeasured bitfield/declarator constructs.

findings.observed: Pointer ordering probes compare full 32-bit numeric addresses unsigned, without physical masking. Short-pointer subtraction lowers to SUB.L plus ASR.L #1: a byte difference of -1 yields -1 rather than signed division's zero. Stored-pointer post-increment writes the advanced pointer before reading the old pointee. The API can express these operations, but the contract lacks explicit rules for these edges and concrete narrow compound/post-increment sequencing.
findings.fix: Document unsigned full-width pointer comparisons separately from 24-bit bus masking; specify observed shift lowering/rounding for power-of-two subtraction and alias-sensitive stored-pointer post-increment order. Add explicit storage-width compound/post-increment patterns; new abstraction is not necessary.

findings.observed: Unchanged example tests pass both a mutation dropping owner-zero attachment and a mutation writing the RAM mirror before all VDP writes. The platform-only trace plus final RAM assertion cannot observe hardware/RAM interleaving. Five other signedness/narrowing/truth mutations are correctly rejected, and actual implementations pass independent source differential checks.
findings.fix: Add owner-zero/self-parent coverage and a shared bus/platform event observer asserting control-high, control-low, data, then RAM mirror. Preserve existing signedness, wrap and negative truth cases.
